# Friends of the Ochils

> Friends of the Ochils (FotO) is a registered Scottish charity (SC022034), founded in 1992, that works to promote and conserve the landscape, natural beauty and wildlife of the Ochil Hills in central Scotland, and to protect the historical and social character of the surrounding communities.

FotO promotes good planning policy, supports responsible public access to the Ochils in line with the Scottish Outdoor Access Code, and encourages study and research relating to the hills and their communities. For nearly 20 years it has responded to planning applications for windfarms and turbines in and around the Ochils, and it also comments on forestry, woodland and other developments. FotO does not campaign against renewable energy; its aim is to protect the Ochils from developments that would harm the landscape and people's enjoyment of it.

- [Latest news](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/latest-news/): FotO's most recent responses, objections and updates, with links to the full documents
- [Windfarms](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/our-work/windfarms/): FotO's involvement in windfarm applications affecting the Ochils
- [Forestry](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/our-work/forestry/): Responses to forestry and woodland creation proposals
- [Other planning issues](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/our-work/other-planning-issues/): Other developments, including the Glenquey Quarry campaign
- [Beauly to Denny Power Line](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/our-work/powerline/): FotO's role in the Beauly to Denny power line inquiry
- [Newsletters](https://www.friendsoftheochils.org.uk/our-work/newsletters/): Member newsletters, annual reviews and financial reports
